provider.name: Shopify
provider.description: Shopify is an e-commerce platform that allows developers to build applications using the GraphQL Admin API and OAuth authentication.

authMethod.text: Apps that run outside the Shopify admin use the authorization code grant: the merchant is redirected to Shopify to approve access, then back to the app with a code that the app exchanges for an access token.
authMethod.quote: for apps that run outside the Shopify admin. The merchant is redirected to Shopify to approve access, then back to your app with a code that your app exchanges for an access token.

difficulty.rationale: Needs client credentials, scope choices, a development store for testing, expiring offline tokens for public apps, and Shopify App Store review if the app is listed publicly.

handsOnEffort.basis: Assumes an existing Shopify store or Partner organization, creating the app in the Dev Dashboard, setting scopes and redirect URLs, and entering the credentials into Composio. Excludes App Store review time.

summary.text: Apps submitted to the Shopify App Store are reviewed by the Shopify app review team before approval.
summary.quote: If you've followed all of the requirements to create your app, then you're ready to submit your app for review by the Shopify app review team.

triggers.text: Submitting the app for a Shopify App Store listing.
triggers.quote: If you've followed all of the requirements to create your app, then you're ready to submit your app for review by the Shopify app review team.

triggers.text: Apps that use customer data must meet Shopify's protected customer data requirements and apply for access in the Partner Dashboard (API access requests > Protected customer data access).
triggers.quote: If your app uses customer data, then you need to meet the protected customer data requirements … and then apply for access to this data in the API access requests > Protected customer data access section of your Partner Dashboard.

publishedTimeline.text: Shopify publishes no review timeline in the retrieved documentation.

prerequisites.text: A Partner organization isn't needed to use the Dev Dashboard: merchants, and developers building for their company's own stores, open it from the Shopify admin. Apps created there are custom apps for that organization's stores.
prerequisites.quote: You don't need a Partner organization to use the Dev Dashboard. If you're a merchant, or a developer building for your company's own stores, then open it from the Shopify admin. … Apps that you create there are custom apps

prerequisites.text: A development store to test the app on; if you don't have one, you can create one.
prerequisites.quote: Development stores can be used to test apps to ensure they're free of bugs or otherwise incomplete. If you don’t have a development store, then you can create one

prerequisites.text: Distribution to the Shopify App Store is still handled in the Partner Dashboard, so listing the app publicly goes through a Partner organization.
prerequisites.quote: To list your app on the Shopify App Store, refer to About distribution … Distribution is still in the Partner Dashboard.

redirectRules.text: Before submitting, the app's App URL and allowed redirection URL must send merchants to the OAuth grant screen as expected.
redirectRules.quote: Before submitting your app, make sure its App URL and allowed redirection URL redirect merchants to the OAuth screen as expected.

model.text: An access scope is a named unit of access that a merchant grants the app, such as read_products or write_orders.
model.quote: A named unit of access that a merchant grants your app, such as read_products or write_orders.

examples.grants: Grants read and write access to orders.
Grants access to read all orders beyond default scope sets.

steps.title: Open the Dev Dashboard in the right organization
steps.action: For an app used only on your own company's stores, open the Dev Dashboard from the Shopify admin (click your store name, then View Dev Dashboard). To list the app on the Shopify App Store, work in a Partner organization, because distribution is in the Partner Dashboard.
steps.where: Shopify admin, or a Partner organization
steps.actorReason: Creating accounts requires human identity and legal agreement.
steps.text: Merchants and developers building for their company's own stores open the Dev Dashboard from the Shopify admin; no Partner organization is needed.
steps.quote: You don't need a Partner organization to use the Dev Dashboard. If you're a merchant, or a developer building for your company's own stores, then open it from the Shopify admin.

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.action: In the Dev Dashboard, create the app. Shopify suggests this path (rather than Shopify CLI) for automation or API-only apps with no UI in the Shopify admin.
steps.actorReason: Developer console actions require a logged-in human user.
steps.text: The Dev Dashboard is the path Shopify suggests for automation or API-only apps with no UI in the Shopify admin.
steps.quote: Best for automation or API-only apps with no UI in the Shopify admin.

steps.title: Check the app URL and redirect URLs
steps.action: In the Dev Dashboard, open Apps, your app, Versions, then the active version, and check the app URL and redirect URLs. The Composio redirect URI is added in a later step.
steps.actorReason: An agent can draft redirect URLs and scope lists, but a human must save them in the console.
steps.text: Check your app URL and your redirect URLs in the active app version settings.
steps.quote: 5. Check your app URL and your redirect URLs. 6. Review and test the URLs that you provided.

steps.title: Obtain Client ID and Client Secret
steps.action: Copy the generated Client ID and Client Secret from your app credentials settings.
steps.actorReason: Viewing and copying secret credentials requires a human operator.
steps.text: Retrieve the Client ID and Client Secret issued when you create your app.
steps.quote: The credentials that identify your app, issued when you create it. The client ID is public. The client secret isn't

steps.title: Create a Custom Auth Config in Composio
steps.action: Create an OAuth2 auth config in Composio and paste your Shopify Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.actorReason: Entering sensitive credentials into Composio requires a human developer.
steps.text: Create the auth config in the Composio dashboard and enter the required credential fields.
steps.quote: 1. Click Create Auth Config 2. Select the toolkit 3. Choose the auth scheme (OAuth2, API Key, Bearer Token, etc.) 4. Follow the dashboard instructions for the required credential fields

steps.title: Add Composio Redirect URI to Shopify App
steps.action: Add the OAuth redirect URI provided by Composio into your allowed redirection URLs in the Shopify Dev Dashboard.
steps.actorReason: An agent can supply the exact URI string, but a human must paste it into the console.
steps.text: For OAuth toolkits, the dashboard shows the redirect URI to add in the provider's developer portal.
steps.quote: For OAuth toolkits, the dashboard shows the redirect URI to add in the provider's developer portal.

steps.title: Test Connection on a Development Store
steps.action: Install your app on a development store to test authentication and API calls.
steps.actorReason: Installing apps on a dev store requires manual human execution.
steps.text: On the app overview page, in the Installs section, click Install app and select the development store.
steps.quote: 4. On the app overview page, in the Installs section, click Install app. 5. Select the development store you wish to use.

steps.title: Submit App for Review (Optional / Public Distribution)
steps.action: Submit your app for approval via the Partner Dashboard if distributing publicly.
steps.actorReason: Submitting applications for formal review is a human-only administrative action.
steps.text: Once the app meets all requirements, submit it for review by the Shopify app review team.
steps.quote: If you've followed all of the requirements to create your app, then you're ready to submit your app for review by the Shopify app review team.

risks.text: New public apps can't use non-expiring offline access tokens for GraphQL Admin API requests, so the integration must handle expiring offline tokens and refresh them.
risks.quote: Non-expiring offline tokens grant permanent access until the app is uninstalled or the secret is revoked. New public apps already can't use them for GraphQL Admin API requests.

risks.text: Apps that are incomplete or have errors that prevent Shopify from reviewing their features won't be approved.
risks.quote: If you submit an app that is incomplete or has errors that prevent us from reviewing its features, then it won't be approved.

risks.text: Existing public apps that still use non-expiring offline tokens are delisted and blocked from new installs on 1 January 2027, and their Admin API requests are rejected from 1 April 2027. This doesn't apply to custom apps or apps created by merchants.
risks.quote: Public apps that still use non-expiring offline access tokens are delisted and blocked from new installs on January 1, 2027. Their GraphQL Admin API and REST Admin API requests are rejected from April 1, 2027. This doesn't apply to custom apps or apps created by merchants.

risks.text: Re-submitting the app slows down the review process.
risks.quote: Resubmitting your app slows down the review process.

faq.question: How do I set up custom OAuth credentials for Shopify?
faq.answer: For a step-by-step guide on creating and configuring your own Shopify OAuth credentials with Composio, see [How to create OAuth credentials for Shopify](https://composio.dev/auth/shopify).

faq.question: Why am I seeing "App not found" when connecting Shopify?
faq.answer: The default Shopify OAuth app may be under review or expired. Use your own OAuth app or API authentication method until the default is restored.

faq.question: Shopify order update 403s can be caused by missing `read_all_orders` scope
faq.answer: Check the scopes on the Shopify connection. If order reads or updates require access beyond the default order scope set, reconnect with the needed order scopes such as `read_all_orders` before retrying.
